The answer is a prediction from the natural quadratic motion model, not a unique consequence of an arbitrary function agreeing with the finite table.

routes.label: Identify the pattern and its assumption

question:
The table below shows the distance \(s\) in feet a ball rolls down an inclined plane in \(t\) seconds.

\[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline t & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5\\ \hline s & 0 & 10 & 40 & 90 & 160 & 250\\ \hline\end{array}\]

The distance \(s\) for \(t=2.5\) is:
solution:
Each listed distance is ten times the square of its listed time. If we assume that the rule \(s=10t^2\) also holds between the listed times, then
\[
s(2.5)=10(2.5)^2=10(6.25)=62.5
\]
feet, giving choice B under that assumption.

The table alone does not force this rule. For example, join each pair of consecutive table points by a straight line segment. This gives a continuous increasing distance function that agrees with every entry. Between \(t=2\) and \(t=3\), its distance increases from \(40\) to \(90\), so its rule there is
\[
s(t)=40+50(t-2).
\]
It gives \(s(2.5)=65\) feet instead. Thus the intermediate distance is not uniquely determined by the stated data; \(62.5\) feet, choice B, requires the additional quadratic-model assumption.
